2027-05-03.title: Monday of the fifth week after Qyomtho
readings: Now is the acceptable time; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything
“I am the light of the world”
2027-05-03.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Fifth Sunday after Qyomtho; Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord, is on Thursday 6 May.
2027-05-03.verse: See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
theo: Three days before Suloko the readings speak of time and of light. St Paul begins with an appeal: “As we work together with him, we urge you also not to accept the grace of God in vain.” Then he quotes the prophet Isaiah, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you,” and turns the old promise into a present fact: “See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!” We are always tempted to place God's time somewhere else: in the past, when we were more fervent, or in the future, when the children are settled, the loan is paid and life is quieter. Paul says no. The day of salvation is today, this Monday morning, with the work and the worries it brings. The Risen Lord does not wait for better circumstances to meet us. In these last days of the fifty days of Qyomtho the Church is preparing to see him ascend and to receive his Spirit; the preparation happens now or it does not happen at all.

Then Paul draws a portrait of the apostolic life, and it is not what anyone would choose. He lists “great endurance, in afflictions, hardships, calamities, beatings, imprisonments, riots, labors, sleepless nights, hunger.” Alongside these he names the weapons of a servant of God: “purity, knowledge, patience, kindness, holiness of spirit, genuine love, truthful speech, and the power of God.” And he ends with a chain of paradoxes that only Easter can explain: “as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything.” How can someone who has nothing possess everything? Only if the one thing he has is Christ, in whom all things hold together. St John Chrysostom, commenting on this passage, said that Paul lists the hardships not to boast but to show that the grace of God was strong enough to carry him through them all (Homilies on 2 Corinthians 12, in substance). The Christian is not someone protected from trouble; he is someone in whom joy survives trouble.

In the Gospel Jesus says in the temple: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life.” He spoke these words, John notes, “in the treasury of the temple,” close to where the great lamps were lit at the feast of Tabernacles. The Pharisees object that he is testifying for himself, and Jesus answers that he does not stand alone: “I testify on my own behalf, and the Father who sent me testifies on my behalf.” The argument is a reminder that faith is not a private opinion; it rests on the witness of the Father to the Son, and soon, at Pentecost, on the witness of the Spirit. Our Church begins each day with the morning prayer of the Shehimo, greeting Christ as the light that has dawned on us. Let the light be practical today: switch off one thing that darkens your mind, open one page of the Gospel, and walk in the light by one honest act. “No one arrested him, because his hour had not yet come.” His hour came on the Cross, and its light still shines from the empty tomb.
outline: Ask: am I waiting for a better time to give myself to God?
Point 1 · Now is the day of salvation
Grace is not to be received in vain; God's time is today.
Paul's paradoxes and the joy that survives trouble.
Point 3 · The light of the world
Following Jesus out of darkness, with the Father's witness.
“See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!”
live: Name one good thing you have been postponing for God, a confession, a visit, a reconciliation, and do it before the week ends.
Turn off one source of darkness in your evening, and read John 8:12 before you sleep.
2027-05-03.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you are the light of the world, and whoever follows you will not walk in darkness. Do not let us receive your grace in vain. Teach us that now is the acceptable time and today the day of salvation. When we are sorrowful, keep us rejoicing; when we are poor, make us rich in you; when we have nothing, let us possess everything by possessing you. Prepare our hearts to see you ascend and to receive your Holy Spirit. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the light of the world comes to us under the humble signs of bread and wine; having nothing in ourselves, we receive everything in him.

quick: Paul: do not receive the grace of God in vain; now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation.
The apostle's life is full of paradox: sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing yet possessing everything.
Jesus says in the temple: I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will have the light of life.
2027-05-03.action: Do today one good thing for God that you have been putting off.
2027-05-03.question: What am I postponing until a better time, when God is asking for it now?

family.explain: Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.” When the power goes off at night, we quickly look for a torch or a lamp, because in the dark we can trip and fall. Sin is like darkness: it makes us lose our way. Jesus is our light: when we follow him, we can see where to walk. St Paul also tells us not to wait: today is the day to be good and to love God.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel lost or sad, that Jesus may be their light.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something good we keep saying we will do later? Can we do it this week?”

illus: A retired schoolteacher in Mavelikara kept a list on her fridge titled “When I have time.” It held visiting her estranged sister, joining the parish prayer group, and learning the evening prayer of the Shehimo by heart. Each year the list grew. During a long stay in hospital she read 2 Corinthians 6:2, and on the morning she came home she crossed out the title and wrote “Now.” Her sister came for lunch that Sunday. They had not spoken for nine years.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, light of the world, shine in our hearts and teach us to answer your grace today. Amen.
share: Do not accept the grace of God in vain (2 Corinthians 6:1). What grace have I received that I am letting go to waste?
As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing (2 Corinthians 6:10). When have I known joy in the middle of sorrow?
Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness (John 8:12). Where do I need Christ's light most today?
pm.resp: Lord, our light and our salvation, hear us.
interc: For those who keep postponing their return to God, that they may hear that today is the day of salvation.
For missionaries and priests who live in hardship, that they may possess everything in Christ.
For the poor who make others rich by their faith and patience.
For those who live in darkness of addiction, despair or sin, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For our parish, as we prepare for Suloko and pray for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the light of the world and testified to him. Let us not receive your grace in vain, but walk in his light today, rejoicing even in sorrow, until we see his glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! St Paul begs the Corinthians: do not accept the grace of God in vain. Then he says: see, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! (2 Corinthians 6:1–2). We like to put God's time in the past or the future. Paul puts it here: today, this Monday, with all its ordinary work.

Paul describes his life as an apostle: afflictions, hardships, beatings, sleepless nights, hunger. And yet he says: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). Only someone who has Christ can say that. Having him, he has everything.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life (John 8:12). He is not one light among many; he is the light by which we see everything else. And his witness is true, because the Father who sent him testifies to him.

In three days we celebrate Suloko, the Ascension, and then we wait for the Holy Spirit. Let us not wait for a better time to turn to God. Today let us do the good we have been postponing, and let us walk in his light. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever been in a room when the lights suddenly went off? It is hard to find the door, and you might bump into a chair. Jesus says: “I am the light of the world.” When we follow Jesus, we do not get lost. St Paul also says something important: “Now is the time!” Don't wait until tomorrow to say sorry or to help someone. Do it today, and Jesus' light will shine through you.

intro: Theme: “See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!”
On Monday of the fifth week after Qyomtho, three days before Suloko: God's today, the riches of the poor apostle, and the light of the world.

points.h: Now is the day of salvation
sub: Preparing now for the Ascension and the Spirit.
q: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you;
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.
points.apply: Write down one thing you have postponed for God and set a day this week to do it.

points.h: Having nothing, and yet possessing everything
q: The Lord is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
I can do all things through him who strengthens me.
points.apply: In one difficulty you face this week, thank God aloud for something he has given you in it.

q: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
but if we walk in the light as he himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.
points.apply: Pray the morning prayer of the Shehimo, or a short morning prayer, each day this week, greeting Christ as your light.

concl: God's time is today; grace postponed is grace wasted.
The one who has Christ has everything and walks in his light.
2027-05-03.resolve: Do today the good you have postponed, rejoice in trouble, and walk in the light of Christ as you prepare for Suloko.
